proof_summary: Lucas-type binomial congruences pair the summands to show that every moment indexed by \(p,\ldots,2p-2\) vanishes modulo \(p\); at index \(p-1\), the first family equals \(1\), while central-binomial divisibility leaves only the middle term in the second family, giving \((-1)^{(p-1)/2}\). Reversing the columns makes each Hankel matrix triangular with this constant diagonal, and combining its product with the reversal sign \((-1)^{(p-1)/2}\) gives the two asserted residues.
